fine_trace.note: The glyph name produced by hb_font_get_glyph_name from the font's post v2 table (attacker-controlled bytes of the input font) is wrapped into the hb_bytes_t object st, whose arrayZ points at the 5-byte stack buffer holding the name.

hb_array_t (and therefore hb_bytes_t, its typedef) overloads operator& to return the underlying data pointer instead of the address of the object; this is the merged hb_bytes_t behaviour the issue describes, and it makes `&st` yield st.arrayZ (the raw name buffer) instead of the hb_bytes_t object address that hb_addressof() (ala std::addressof()) would return.

fine_trace.code: const uint16_t *gid = (const uint16_t *) hb_bsearch_r (&st, gids, count, sizeof (gids[0]), cmp_key, (void *) this);
fine_trace.note: `&st` invokes the overloaded operator&, so the key pointer handed to hb_bsearch_r is st.arrayZ - the glyph-name bytes living in the 5-byte stack buffer - rather than the address of the hb_bytes_t object.
hb_bsearch_r forwards the forged key pointer unchanged to the user comparator cmp_key during each probe of the sorted glyph-id array.

cmp_key reinterprets the stack-resident glyph-name bytes as an hb_bytes_t; reading key->arrayZ and key->len through *key dereferences memory at and beyond the 5-byte buffer (key->len lies 8 bytes into it).

cmp dereferences the forged hb_bytes_t: evaluating a.len performs a 4-byte load 8 bytes into the 5-byte stack buffer, producing the ASAN stack-buffer-overflow READ 4; had the lengths matched, hb_memcmp would have dereferenced the forged key->arrayZ pointer.

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: The public issue states that taking the address of hb_bytes_t directly is not possible after the hb_bytes_t merge and that hb_addressof() (ala std::addressof()) must be used. In src/hb-ot-post-table.hh get_glyph_from_name the code does `hb_bsearch_r (&st, ...)` where st is an hb_bytes_t; because hb_array_t overloads operator& to return arrayZ, the search key becomes the raw glyph-name bytes instead of the object address, and cmp_key reinterprets those bytes as an hb_bytes_t, causing the out-of-bounds read in hb_array_t::cmp (ASAN stack-buffer-overflow READ 4). The upstream fix (commit 8d2d41025619e24160ed80edd1c413168a2dda36) adds hb_addressof() and changes the call to `hb_bsearch_r (hb_addressof (st), ...)`.
